strengths: Clear problem motivation: Figure 1 provides compelling evidence for fundamental differences between language and visual tokens (inter/intra-class distance 19.283 vs 0.748), well-explaining why MoE fails in DiT

Well-structured and intuitive technical approach: Two-step router elegantly addresses both functional heterogeneity (conditional routing) and spatial redundancy (prototypical routing with learnable prototypes)

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive comparisons on ImageNet across multiple settings (dense/MoE baselines, DDPM/Rectified Flow, CFG=1.0/1.5, multiple model sizes S/B/L/XL) with thorough ablations

Strong empirical results: Consistently outperforms baselines with parameter efficiency; ProMoE-L achieves FID 2.79 (CFG=1.5) vs 3.56 for Dense-DiT-L with same activated parameters; surpasses DiffMoE with 1.7× fewer total parameters
Excellent reproducibility: Clear implementation details, promises code release, provides implementation algorithm, comprehensive ablations (Tables 6-13) validating each component

Well-written and clear: Good organization with effective visualizations (Figures 1, 2, 6 showing token distribution, architecture, and expert assignments); t-SNE visualizations effectively demonstrate clustering quality
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components are relatively standard applications—conditional routing is a natural consequence of CFG, prototypical routing uses straightforward learnable prototypes with cosine similarity, and RCL is essentially an InfoNCE-style contrastive loss; main contribution is in combination rather than fundamental innovation

Narrow evaluation scope: Limited to ImageNet 256×256 class-conditional generation only; no text-to-image, higher resolutions, or other datasets; generalizability to different generation tasks and modalities remains unknown

Incomplete semantic guidance analysis: Section 4.2 uses manually partitioned superclasses (ad-hoc approach), K-means baseline has known sensitivity issues, and lacks deeper investigation into why explicit semantic guidance helps beyond spatial redundancy reasoning

Significant memory overhead underexplored: Total parameters ~2.3× higher than dense models (e.g., 300M vs 130M activated); limited discussion of actual wall-clock training time, memory requirements, or practical computational costs vs. dense models

Limited expert interpretability: Figure 6 shows clustering quality but lacks analysis of what experts actually specialize in; no visualization of learned prototypes or their evolution; missing analysis of whether assignments align with semantic content

Hyperparameter choices not well-justified: Key parameters (τ=0.07, α=1) lack ablation or justification; identity vs softmax activation shows large gap (Table 7) but deserves deeper investigation; activation function comparison shows surprising results (identity>>sigmoid>softmax) without explanation

Methodological concerns: Load-balancing loss disabled in key experiments (Table 1) to isolate routing effects, making MoE baseline comparisons less direct; RCL operates on mini-batch assignments which could be noisy early in training; CFG-specific design with unclear generalization to other guidance methods

Incomplete technical analysis: Limited discussion of RCL interaction with shared/unconditional experts during training; inference without CFG raises questions about whether unused unconditional experts represent wasted capacity

Evaluation limitations: No human evaluation or perceptual metrics (LPIPS, DINO); FID/IS acknowledged as potentially missing fine-grained quality; generated samples (Figure 4) look good visually but lack formal quality assessment; no actual wall-clock time or memory measurements provided

Large performance gaps with baselines raise fairness questions: DiT-MoE, EC-DiT, DiffMoE gaps are substantial (Table 5: FID 13.55 vs 11.61); whether this reflects implementation differences, hyperparameter tuning, or fundamental advantages needs clarification

strengths: Clear problem motivation with compelling evidence (Figure 1) showing fundamental differences between language and visual tokens
Comprehensive experimental validation across DDPM and Rectified Flow objectives, multiple model sizes, with consistent improvements and fair parameter matching
Strong empirical results demonstrating that ProMoE-L outperforms Dense-DiT-XL with fewer activated parameters (458M vs 675M)
Well-designed two-step routing approach that naturally follows from CFG architecture and is well-suited for vision
Thorough ablation studies (Table 6) validating each component's contribution to overall performance
Extensive supplementary analysis including t-SNE visualizations, algorithm descriptions, and reproducibility statements
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: conditional routing is straightforward CFG-based hard routing, prototypical routing resembles standard prototype clustering, and routing contrastive loss follows standard contrastive learning—contribution is primarily in combination rather than innovation

Severely narrow evaluation scope restricted to ImageNet 256×256 class-conditional generation only; no evaluation at higher resolutions, text-to-image, video, or other modalities despite claiming general vision relevance
Method design is tailored to specific CFG-based diffusion setting; unclear how conditional routing generalizes to diffusion models without explicit CFG separation or other conditioning mechanisms

Shallow analysis of why the approach works: expert diversity measured superficially via SVD, limited investigation of what experts learn, and lack of rigorous connection between diagnosed problems (spatial redundancy) and proposed solutions
Incomplete computational analysis: no wall-clock training time comparisons, memory overhead of prototypes/routing not quantified, inference cost with routing computation not discussed
Identity activation choice over softmax lacks theoretical justification and is validated only empirically; hyperparameter sensitivity (τ=0.07, λ_RCL) partially unexplored

Baseline comparison concerns: architectural differences despite equivalent activated parameters, concurrent work (DiffMoE) comparison fairness unclear, limited discussion of why existing MoE designs fail conceptually
Statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing reported for claimed improvements

strengths: Clear and insightful problem analysis: Figure 1 compellingly demonstrates fundamental differences between language and visual tokens, motivating each design component with concrete reasoning

Principled two-step routing design: Conditional routing naturally addresses classifier-free guidance, prototypical routing is semantically aligned, and routing contrastive loss elegantly enforces specialization without manual labels

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive comparisons across dense baselines and MoE SOTAs, dual training objectives (DDPM and Rectified Flow), multiple model scales, thorough ablations, and scaling experiments

Strong empirical results: Consistent improvements across all settings (24.8% FID reduction for L-Flow at cfg=1.0), outperforms larger baselines (ProMoE-L-Flow 1.063B surpasses DiffMoE-L-Flow 1.846B), faster convergence demonstrated
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Clear figures with good intuitions, detailed implementation algorithms, comprehensive appendix, and promise of code/model release
Practical significance: Addresses scalability of widely-used DiT architecture with parameter-efficient improvements directly applicable to real-world model training
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components apply existing techniques straightforwardly (learnable prototypes, standard contrastive learning, CFG-based engineering). Novelty is primarily in combination and application rather than fundamental new methods

Narrow evaluation scope: Single dataset (ImageNet-1K), single resolution (256×256), single task (class-conditional only), no text-to-image or higher resolutions tested. Generalization claims somewhat overstated given these constraints

Shallow expert specialization analysis: Figure 1(b) shows diversity improves, but no analysis of what individual experts learn. Missing visualizations of expert-specific token patterns, load balancing effects, or semantic specialization details
Incomplete computational analysis: Missing actual runtime/wall-clock comparisons despite overhead from prototypical routing and RCL. Memory efficiency and inference speed not discussed

Semantic guidance design limitations: Explicit guidance requires manual class partitioning (dataset-specific, not generalizable). K-means supports only top-1 assignment. Jump to RCL as solution feels somewhat ad-hoc

Modest improvements in some settings: DDPM results show smaller gains (ProMoE-B-DDPM 17.90 vs Dense 18.61 at cfg=1.5). Relative improvements less pronounced than Rectified Flow, and benefits diminish with stronger guidance

Hyperparameter sensitivity underexplored: Only RCL loss weight ablated (Table 13). Other hyperparameters (temperature τ, scaling factor α, expert count) not thoroughly analyzed. Design choices (identity activation, cosine similarity) not fully justified

Limited theoretical understanding: No convergence analysis or theoretical justification. Connection between expert metrics (intra-coherence/inter-diversity) and generation quality lacks rigor. Why the approach fundamentally solves visual token redundancy not deeply explained

strengths: Well-motivated analysis of language vs. visual token differences with compelling empirical evidence (Figure 1: inter-to-intra class distance ratio 19.28 vs 0.748)
Clear and well-justified two-step routing design elegantly addressing functional heterogeneity and semantic variation in visual tokens
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple model sizes (S/B/L/XL), training objectives (DDPM, Rectified Flow), and downstream tasks (ImageNet, text-to-image)
Strong and consistent empirical results: ProMoE-L-Flow surpasses Dense-DiT-XL-Flow on FID with fewer activated parameters; 19.7-20.5% FID reduction vs DiffMoE-L
Thorough ablation studies validating each component (Tables 7-9) with clear improvements at each step
Practical efficiency: comparable or better training/inference time and FLOPs than baselines, demonstrating gains from methodology
Excellent presentation with clear figures, comprehensive appendix with algorithms, and reproducibility artifacts (code/models promised, detailed hyperparameters)
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual components: conditional routing (hard-routing based on CFG), prototypical routing (learnable prototypes with cosine similarity), and contrastive loss are all standard techniques; contribution is primarily in their integration

Strong dependence on classifier-free guidance paradigm: conditional routing requires paired conditional/unconditional samples at training time, limiting generalization to unconditional generation or domains without natural splits

Weak theoretical justification: connection between proposed components and expert specialization objectives (intra-expert coherence, inter-expert diversity) appears post-hoc; identity activation's claimed stability lacks investigation; optimal choice of cosine similarity not justified

Incomplete semantic guidance analysis (Section 4.2): limited baseline methods (classification and k-means); unfair RCL comparison (end-to-end training vs isolated baselines); no analysis of what semantic properties prototypes capture

Evaluation limitations: no human evaluation despite acknowledging FID/IS may not capture fine-grained quality; scope limited to 256×256 ImageNet; text-to-image evaluated on small LAION subset; no evaluation on other vision generative tasks (video, 3D)

Underexplored technical details: online centroid computation in RCL could be noisy with small batches; fine-grained expert segmentation (factor of 2) is aggressive with unanalyzed impact; prototype initialization not specified; no ablation for temperature τ=0.07

Fairness concerns in comparisons: different expert configurations (ProMoE E14A1S1U1 vs baselines E8A1S0U0), unconditional expert is ProMoE-specific, RCL loss not used by baselines; more discussion needed

Load-balancing mechanism inadequately analyzed: claim that RCL's push-away acts as load-balancing needs deeper investigation; adding explicit load-balancing loss degrades performance without clear explanation (Table 17)
Limited scope: primarily image generation domain; unclear if approach generalizes to unconditional generation or other vision tasks; no analysis of failure cases or when ProMoE underperforms

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with empirical evidence (Figure 1) showing token distribution differences between language and vision models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple training objectives (DDPM, Rectified Flow), model scales (S/B/L/XL), and generation tasks with thorough ablations
Consistent empirical improvements (15-20% FID reduction) across diverse settings with detailed expert utilization analysis
Clear presentation with good visualizations and commitment to code release with reproducibility details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: prototypical routing is essentially learnable clustering, routing contrastive loss is straightforward application of existing techniques, conditional routing is simple architectural choice—contributions feel incremental rather than fundamental

Critical fairness concerns in baseline comparisons: classification-based routing (5.91 FID, Table 1) vastly outperforms DiT-MoE (8.94 FID) and DiffMoE (8.22 FID) by 30-40%, suggesting potential implementation issues or unfair evaluation setup; ProMoE-B (6.39 FID) is only marginally better than the classification baseline

Insufficient justification for key design choices: identity activation function lacks explanation (why not learned scaling?); hard conditional routing not ablated (why not soft routing?); prototype initialization not clearly specified

Confusing relationship between components: explicit classification guidance outperforms final RCL method; unclear why RCL adds value when Table 7 shows modest 1-2 FID improvement and Section 4.2's classification baseline is superior
Semantic guidance still requires label information for conditional vs. unconditional token separation, departing from unsupervised routing and creating unfair comparison with baselines
Limited analysis of learned expert specialization: Figure 6 shows utilization differs from baselines but provides no evidence of meaningful pattern specialization or generalization across datasets

Incremental empirical gains: 15-20% FID improvements are consistent but modest for a top-tier venue; evaluation metric limitations acknowledged (FID/IS may not capture perceptual quality) undermine confidence

Architectural fairness issues: ProMoE uses 14 total experts vs. baselines' 8 experts, sometimes with more total parameters; missing comparison with dense model scaling at equivalent parameter count to demonstrate MoE necessity

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Figure 1 provides compelling evidence that visual tokens have 25× lower semantic density than language tokens, clearly justifying the need for explicit routing guidance
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple model scales (S/B/L/XL), two training paradigms (DDPM, Rectified Flow), extensive comparisons with dense and MoE baselines, and thorough ablations
Strong empirical results: ProMoE-L outperforms Dense-DiT-XL at same activated parameters (FID 2.79 vs 3.23 at CFG=1.5) and surpasses larger models (1.063B params vs DiffMoE-L's 1.846B)
Expert specialization validation: Figure 6 clearly demonstrates ProMoE achieves meaningful specialization vs poor specialization in baselines
Practical efficiency: Better performance than DiffMoE with lower inference time and comparable GFLOPs
Thorough reproducibility: Detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, promised code release, extensive appendices
Generalization demonstrated: Text-to-image experiments validate approach beyond class-conditional generation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components (conditional routing, prototypical routing, contrastive loss) are straightforward applications of existing techniques. Contribution is primarily in combination rather than novel methods

Insufficient mechanistic justification: Why prototypical routing specifically helps visual tokens lacks deep explanation. Identity activation (Table 8) suggests direct similarity matching—unclear what learned prototypes add beyond static clustering
Conditional routing lacks generalizability: Tightly coupled to classifier-free guidance in diffusion models; doesn't generalize to other vision models or tasks

Routing contrastive loss appears ad-hoc: Prototypical routing alone shows FID 7.92 vs 6.39 with RCL (Table 7), indicating the core mechanism doesn't naturally enforce semantic clustering. RCL feels like a patch rather than principled solution
Incomplete experimental justification: Table 1 shows classification-based guidance outperforms ProMoE (FID 5.91 vs 6.39), but dismissal of generalization concerns is not empirically validated
Limited theoretical understanding: Shallow explanation of why explicit routing guidance overcomes visual token redundancy; no analysis of what prototypes learn or how they specialize
Missing statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; no multiple runs reported despite stochasticity in training
Minimal failure case analysis: Lacks discussion of when ProMoE underperforms, scalability to small models, or when additional complexity isn't justified
Insufficient hyperparameter ablation: Temperature, scaling factor α, and other design choices not thoroughly ablated
